sources.title: Anne-Maria Fehn, Beatriz Amorim and Jorge Rocha, The linguistic and genetic landscape of southern Africa, Journal of Anthropological Sciences (2022)
sources.note: Indexed scholarly text checked for the three distinct families Kx’a, Tuu and Khoe-Kwadi, and diversity within Khoe-Kwadi. Direct PDF returned cache miss. This is a linguistic classification, not permission to identify archaeological peoples from DNA or to map one ethnic state.

sources.title: Palaeoproteomics confirm earliest domesticated sheep in southern Africa ca. 2000 BP, Scientific Reports (2021)
sources.note: Direct original research read. Protein identification confirms the Spoegrivier phalanx as sheep; direct radiocarbon age 2105 ± 65 BP with calibration ranges 351 to 308 BCE (4.8%) or 197 BCE to 110 CE (90.7%). Public rounded age avoids converting an uncalibrated BP date directly to an exact calendar year.

sources.title: Tammy Hodgskiss, Fascinating Technologies Used by the San People of Southern Africa, Origins Centre, University of the Witwatersrand
sources.note: Direct museum exhibit read. Sections 2, 4, 5 and 6 describe composite arrows, adhesive, eggshell containers and digging sticks. Displayed arrowheads and digging stick are labeled 1970. No universal dating of these objects to 4000 BCE; no medicinal efficacy claim or poison recipe reproduced.

sources.title: Peabody Museum, Ostrich egg, water carrier?, object 58-43-50/10278
sources.note: Indexed complete museum object record read; direct access returned an error. Described as perforated at one end, collected by the Peabody Southwest Africa Expedition in spring/summer 1958; provenance near Gautsche Pan and Kai Kai. Catalogue title includes a question mark, preserved as attribution rather than an unqualified archaeological identification.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Richtersveld Cultural and Botanical Landscape
sources.note: Direct institutional text read. Living Nama pastoral landscape with communal grazing, stockposts, portable rush-mat houses, medicinal plant collection and oral traditions. Inscribed 2007. Its long-term cultural comparison is not used as proof that every modern house detail was present at an exact prehistoric date.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Tsodilo
sources.note: Full indexed institutional text read. Over 4500 paintings, long but discontinuous archaeology, broad and uncertain art dates, living sacred landscape of both San and Hambukushu communities. No claim that all paintings are San or that the full 100000-year sequence has one known ethnic identity.

sources.title: University of Cape Town, The story-telling project (2011)
sources.note: Direct text read. Lloyd and Bleek recorded in the 1870s and 1880s, publication in 1911, and the contribution of ||kabbo after his release from the Breakwater Convict Station.

sources.title: Pippa Skotnes, ǃnanni, Tamme, |uma and Da, Digital Bleek and Lloyd (2025)
sources.note: Direct curator research and primary archive links read. Opening account of |uma’s family cites LL121:10105v and LL122:10225 to 52v. Later sections document the boys’ drawings, plant knowledge, play huts, and dates at Mowbray. Violence is summarized without graphic details; no claim that these four boys represent all San childhoods.

sources.title: South African Government, National Coat of Arms
sources.note: Full indexed official page read; direct fetch returned error. Launch 27 April 2000. Exact public form !ke e: /xarra //ke with official translation diverse people unite. Explicitly a modern commemorative motto using /Xam, not an ancient inscription or a surviving sentence spoken in 1530. Source’s loose label Khoisan language is not repeated as a genealogical claim.

sources.title: South African San Institute, San Code of Research Ethics (2017)
sources.note: Direct four-page original community document read. Respect, honesty, justice/fairness, care and process; community involvement, plain-language explanation, benefit sharing and privacy. No claim that one South African council represents every San community in southern Africa.

proposedOverrides.name: Khoisan
proposedOverrides.summary: Diverse Khoe and San peoples with distinct languages, livelihoods and continuing histories.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Standalone umbrella-label explanation. Some imported snapshots extend from West/Central Africa into the Horn and southern Africa, so public opening explicitly rejects this as a defensible unified territory. No ethnic or political association with bantu, bantu-peoples, or any modern state. Modern examples are individually dated or labeled living traditions, not back-projected into the imported interval.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Officially attested modern national motto in |Xam, with official translation and explicit 2000 date; no claim of a prehistoric script or textual witness.
